newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: REMY TO DOUBLE ASIA CHAMPAGNE SALES.
newsitem.headline: REMY TO DOUBLE ASIA CHAMPAGNE SALES.

text.p: French drinks group Remy-Cointreau (Remy) plans to double sales of its premium champagne brands in Asia by the millennium, an executive told Reuters on Thursday.
"We want to double champagne exports to Asia over the next four years," Denis Vergneau, international brand manager with Remy's Champagne P&C Heidsieck unit.
Remy, whose brands include Piper-Heidsieck and Charles Heidsieck, said this would represent about 12 percent of the company's total champagne production, presently about 13 million bottles.
Industry experts estimate that Asia, excluding Australia, now consumes more than 3.5 million bottles of champagne each year, but this figure is growing rapidly.
The French champagne industry exports about 100 million bottles annually.
Vergneau was in Singapore for the Asia relaunch of Piper-Heidsieck, a Remy marque which has been re-branded in red to distinguish it from competing products.
He said Australia, Japan, Hong Kong and Singapore had great potential, but the key to expansion was China.
"There is very good growth potential in Asia, but especially China. No one knows what's going to happen in China," Vergneau said.
Remy-Cointreau has been active in China for about 15 years where it produces its Dynasty range of wines.
About 20 million bottles in the Dynasty range are sold in China every year, Vergneau said.
